The C-only model (which sees the context but not the question) scores almost nothing on MuSiQue-Ans. Two sets of numbers are reported:

| Split | Answer F1 (An) | Support F1 (Sp) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Validation | 3.4 | 0.0 | Table 4, p. 11 |
| Test | 3.7 | 0.0 | Table 5, p. 11 |

Table 5 reports test-set numbers for MuSiQue-Ans and MuSiQue-Full, while all other results are on the validation set (p. 10).

**Comparison with other datasets (Table 4, p. 11):**
- On HotpotQA (HQ-20K), C-only gets 18.4 An and 67.6 Sp.
- On 2WikiMultihopQA (2W-20K), it gets 50.1 An and 92.0 Sp.
- The authors note that support identification on those datasets "can be done to a surprisingly high degree (67.6 and 92.0 F1) even without the question (C-only model), but fails on MuSiQue-Ans" (p. 11).

**Related figures:**
- On MuSiQue-Full, C-only gets 1.6 An+Sf and 1.1 Sp+Sf (Table 5, p. 11).
- Without the Disconnection Filter, C-only rises to 8.6 An and 22.4 Sp. Without the Reduced Train-Test Leakage split, it rises to 69.5 An and 42.3 Sp (Table 6, p. 11).
- The low support score depends on the "positive distractors" used to build the context. With 20 distractor paragraphs drawn from full Wikipedia instead, C-only would reach 12.4 An and 66.4 Sp (Table 7, p. 12).
